evals.prompt: Plan a new 24-second faceless Hyperframes feature video for Crator about a small electronics distributor: bring in a stock CSV, configure replenishment, route a purchase order to the manager, and show the approved order. It will be watched on LinkedIn/X. We want it polished and visually interesting. The CTA is Start your free trial at cratorlabs.ai. No pricing or implementation-time claims are confirmed. Give a concrete timed direction with camera, object, color and handoff decisions plus a short verification plan. Do not generate a video or edit any project. Keep the answer under 700 words.
evals.expected_output: A fresh causal business story with useful native ERP views, varied smooth motion, feed readability and a coherent ending; no unconfirmed claims or mechanical reuse of furniture/Lovable/orbit.
assertions: Tracks one identifiable item or order across multiple actions, ending in its changed native state.
Specifies at least three different scene actions or camera mechanisms rather than repeating one progress layout.
Names relevant inventory/replenishment and purchase-order UI, rather than a generic dashboard.
Includes a feed-size readability check and a check of changed scene boundaries.
Does not assert unconfirmed price/time claims or prescribe the old Lovable/furniture/orbit sequence.

evals.prompt: Review this Crator Hyperframes edit concept and give concrete fixes, under 650 words. Current cut: every progress beat has a permanent top-left title, a big frontal UI card below, 0/3 changing to 3/3, and the same 0.5s zoom. Inventory, accounting and manufacturing all use the Sales Order page. The ERP word changes weight across the opening. A large Approved checkmark/text group is left aligned inside a centered 1520px container at top 317 on a 1920x1080 canvas. The final logo/CTA/URL is three widely separated blocks high on screen, and the incoming trial headline is reused on the last frame. The user says it still feels like a PPT, wants more visual interest, the Approved scene centered, and half a second less on the bill. They like the existing music and the composer. Explain what you would change and preserve, with concrete choreography and technical checks. Do not generate a video or edit project files.
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis of causal-story/composition issue rather than more effects; native module fixes, measured grouped centering, preserved composer/music, timing ripple and matched closing boundary.
assertions: Replaces the repeated title/card/counter structure with a causal product sequence, preserving the liked composer and music.
Maps inventory, accounting and manufacturing to distinct relevant native ERP views.
Centers checkmark and Approved text as one group rather than merely centering its container.
Updates both the final CTA group and its incoming matched geometry to prevent a seam jump.
The half-second bill trim updates later starts, total duration, audio endpoint and continuity ledger rather than speeding every scene.
